findings.trigger_condition: Input graph contains a large number of distinct node values that are unhashable (lists, dicts, sets), or a mix of many unhashable and hashable nodes. Every _id_of() call then linearly scans all previously registered nodes: the unhashable path scans unhashable_ids and hashable_ids (lines 63-72), and even the hashable fast path rescans the entire unhashable_ids list on every lookup (lines 83-87).
findings.root_cause: Node deduplication relies on flat, linear registration lists (unhashable_ids / hashable_ids) with equality scans instead of mapping each value to a canonical hashable key (e.g., a recursive freeze to tuple/frozenset) for O(1) dict lookup. Registration is therefore O(n) per node and O(n^2) total, and every single comparison is a full __eq__ over the value contents.
findings.impact: Measured quadratic scaling: all-unhashable fan graph 0.032s @ 1k nodes, 0.131s @ 2k, 0.565s @ 4k, 2.004s @ 8k; mixed hashable/unhashable graph 0.094s @ 1k up to 6.212s @ 8k (both ~4x per doubling). Large unhashable-node inputs (e.g., 20k-50k nodes) take tens of seconds to minutes and will time out or fail any performance budget; the 'very deep/large acyclic input' requirement is only met for the layering pass, not for node registration.
findings.suggested_validation: Build dependency_layers from a chain/fan of N distinct unhashable values (e.g., lists [i]) for N in {2k,4k,8k,16k} and assert near-linear wall-clock growth, or time-box a >=10k-unhashable-node graph. A canonicalization fix (recursively freezing lists/dicts/sets into hashable forms, then using a dict for lookup) should make both cases O(n).

findings.trigger_condition: Any node value whose __eq__ returns a non-bool object or raises, e.g. numpy arrays (unhashable, so they take the linear-scan path) or a custom class with a pathological __eq__. _same_node returns `left is right or left == right` and the result is truthiness-coerced by the surrounding if-statements.
findings.root_cause: _same_node passes the raw == result straight into a boolean context; for numpy arrays, array == array yields an array and bool(array) raises ValueError ('truth value ... ambiguous'). Because the cross-registry scans (lines 63-72 and 83-87) force an equality comparison between every hashable and every unhashable node on each lookup, any __eq__ that raises or returns a non-bool anywhere in the graph aborts the entire call, even for node types whose equality is never meant to be consulted.
findings.impact: Deterministic crash on common value types: reproduced ValueError with `dependency_layers([(np.array([1,2]), 0), (np.array([1,2]), 0)])`. A single hostile/odd __eq__ among nodes or a common non-bool-equality type (numpy, pandas) fails the whole graph build.
findings.suggested_validation: Call dependency_layers with numpy arrays and with objects whose __eq__ returns a non-bool (or raises) as nodes and assert it completes instead of raising. Fix by coercing the comparison result with bool() (or catching exceptions from == and falling back to identity-only matching) inside _same_node.
